name: Leiden University Excellence Scholarship (LExS)
requiredDocuments: A completed online application for admission to a full-time Leiden University Master's programme (the application fee, if applicable, must be paid)
LExS motivation letter — a PDF of max. 500 words explaining why you should be considered for the award, uploaded in the Scholarships section of the online admission application

Evidence of excellent prior academic results relevant to the chosen Master's (as part of the admission application; an indication is top ~10% of graduates of the previous programme, though proof of ranking is not required)

timeline.resultsBy: Before the end of April (after the 1 December deadline); faculty committees nominate within 6 weeks of the deadline
timeline.notes: Dates are for the September 2027 intake (the cycle open as of June 2026). Deadline of 1 December 2026 confirmed on both the LExS page and the scholarships listing page on 2026-06-18. The LExS applies only to programmes starting in September; programmes starting in February are excluded.

benefits: A fixed contribution toward the tuition fee only, at one of five award levels: EUR 10,000, EUR 15,000, EUR 17,500, EUR 18,500, or EUR 19,000
Awarded for the full duration of the Master's study programme
The award level is final and non-negotiable once granted

acceptanceRate.estimateNote: No acceptance rate is published. The official page states there are 'around 25 LExS scholarships available each year, while over a thousand students apply' — implying very roughly ~2.5% of applicants, but the university does not publish a figure. Source: https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/scholarships/sea/leiden-university-excellence-scholarship-lexs (accessed 2026-06-18).

mustKnow: NOT a full scholarship: the official page states verbatim 'The LExS is not a full scholarship and does not cover the full cost of your studies' — it is a partial contribution to tuition only (EUR 10,000-19,000), with no living stipend, travel, or insurance. 'A significant personal contribution will be required.'
Highly competitive: only around 25 awards per year against over a thousand applicants.

Two-step: you must FIRST submit a complete online application for admission to a Master's programme, then the LExS option appears in the Scholarships section of that application — you cannot apply for the scholarship independently.

Nationality gate: applicants must hold a non-EEA/non-EFTA passport and not be eligible for Dutch student finance (Studiefinanciering). Bangladesh qualifies. EXCEPTION: for all LLM Advanced Studies programmes and the MSc in International Relations and Diplomacy, no nationality restriction applies.

Programme exclusions: not available for Leiden Law School's LLM (non-advanced) and MSc programmes, for any programme starting in February, or to applicants who already hold a Leiden University Master's degree (with limited LLM Advanced Studies exceptions).

Cannot be combined with another FULL external scholarship; recipients must notify the Scholarships department if they receive other full funding. A partial external scholarship may be combinable in some cases.
Visa requirement remains: as a non-EEA recipient you must still submit 'proof of sufficient funds' for your student visa/residence permit application — the LExS alone does not satisfy this.

Late or incomplete applications are not considered; both the admission application and the scholarship application must be submitted before the 1 December deadline (allow up to 3 working days to create/submit the admission application).

duration: Duration of the Master's programme (typically 1-2 years)
eligibleNationalities: Non-EEA/non-EFTA passport holders who are not eligible for Dutch student finance (Studiefinanciering). Bangladesh is eligible. EEA = all EU countries plus Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland (these are NOT eligible). Exception: no nationality restriction for all LLM Advanced Studies programmes and the MSc in International Relations and Diplomacy.
